statement: $P\in AB$, $Q\in AC$ of $\triangle ABC$ with $BP=CQ$; circumcircles of $\triangle BPR$ and $\triangle CQR$ (where $R=BQ\cap CP$) meet again at $S$. Prove $S$ lies on the bisector of $\angle BAC$.

A cycle on an $n\times n$ board is a sequence of $\geq 4$ distinct squares where consecutive squares share a side. A mischievous set intersects every cycle. Find all $C$ such that for each $n$, there is a mischievous set with $\leq Cn^2$ squares.
Integers $a_1<a_2<\cdots<a_n$ with $1<a_1$ and $a_n<2a_1$. If $m$ = number of distinct prime factors of $a_1\cdots a_n$, prove $(a_1\cdots a_n)^{m-1}\geq(n!)^m$.
Prove $\mathbb{Z}^+$ can be partitioned into 5 distinct subsets such that for every $n$, the 5-tuple $(n,2n,3n,4n,5n)$ contains exactly one element from each subset.

Isosceles $\triangle ABC$ ($AB=AC$); $M$ = midpoint of $BC$; $D$ = projection of $M$ on $AB$; circle $\omega$ inscribed in $\triangle ACD$ tangent to $AD,AC$ at $K,L$; tangent lines to $\omega$ from $M$ meet $KL$ at $X,Y$ (with $X,K,L,Y$ in order). Prove $M,D,X,Y$ are concyclic.

Sequences $(a_0,\ldots,a_n)$, $(b_0,\ldots,b_n)$, $(c_0,\ldots,c_{2n})$ of nonneg­ative reals with $a_ib_j\leq(c_{i+j})^2$ for all $0\leq i,j\leq n$. Prove $\left(\sum_{i=0}^n a_i\right)\left(\sum_{j=0}^n b_j\right)\leq\left(\sum_{k=0}^{2n}c_k\right)^2$.
